svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Polaris Distributed SQL Query Engine
svg.desc: SQL enters a front end and two-phase optimizer. DQP turns the plan into a task DAG. Finite-state orchestration and a global scheduler place work on stateless compute. Tasks operate over data cells whose durable state remains in remote storage.
svg.text: Polaris — Distributed SQL Query Engine (Fabric Warehouse / SQL Analytics Endpoint)
Query plan → DAG of task templates
Each task: input cells + template + output cells
FIFO + best-fit placement on idle capacity
Tasks re-encoded as T-SQL for local SQL Server
Union of all active query DAGs
States: Ready / Run / Blocked / Failed / Success
Transient failures retried at task level
BACK-END COMPUTE POOL (stateless SQL Server nodes)
DQP sees cells only; local engine reads
ONELAKE — Remote Durable State (data · metadata · transaction logs)
Delta Lake / Parquet files · shared across Warehouse and SQL Analytics Endpoint · compute is stateless — caches rebuilt lazily from persisted data
Cache loss never fails in-flight work · partial query restarts supported · same task engine serves query and ingest paths

g.title: SQL front end — The SQL front end parses and optimizes a query before distributed execution.
Distributed optimizer — A second planning phase chooses distribution properties and minimizes data movement.
Task DAG — DQP divides the physical plan into tasks linked by dataflow and precedence.
FSM orchestration — Hierarchical state machines track query, template, and task progress and retry.
Global workload scheduler — A workload graph schedules tasks across concurrent queries by multidimensional resource demand.
Stateless compute pool — Compute nodes run task templates while durable state remains external.
Data cells and storage — Two-dimensional cells connect partition pruning and hash distribution to durable data.
